BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                              OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI

    In the Matter of Union Electric Company           §
    d/b/a Ameren Missouri's Tariffs to Adjust Its     §              No. ER-2026-0291
                                                      §
    Revenues for Electric Service                     §

      SIERRA CLUB’S RESPONSE IN SUPPORT OF CONSUMERS COUNCIL OF
MISSOURI’S MOTION FOR ADDITIONAL LOCAL PUBLIC HEARING IN THE CITY
                           OF ST. LOUIS

          Sierra Club respectfully requests that the Commission grant the Consumers Council of

Missouri’s Motion for Additional Local Public Hearing in the City of St. Louis.1 Sierra Club

further requests that this additional in-person local public hearing be held in the North side of the

City of St. Louis, such as the O’Fallon Park Rec Complex.2 This community is currently saddled

with multiple unique challenges that create an acute need for a public hearing that is close enough

for individuals living in these communities to be afforded the opportunity to be heard. That need

is particularly salient in a case where Ameren in proposing double-digit percentage rate increases

for residential electric customers.


          First, the citizens of the North side of St. Louis are disproportionately energy burdened and

therefore would be well-served by a local hearing to express their concerns regarding this ongoing

issue. Energy burden is the percentage of a household’s annual income that is spent on energy

utility bills.3 Renew Missouri has tracked and mapped the energy burdens on different Census




1
 Motion for Additional Public Hearing in the City of St. Louis, Consumers Council of Missouri (Filed
10/16/2026), In the Matter of Union Electric Company d/b/a Ameren Missouri’s Tariffs to Adjust its
Revenues for Electric Service, MO PSC Case No. ER-2026-0291, EFIS Item No. 58.
2
    The O’Fallon Park Rec Complex is located at 4343 W Florissant Ave, St. Louis, MO 63115.
3
   Jenn DeRose & Tori Cheatham, St. Louis Energy Burden Report at 5, Sierra Club (2025)
https://www.sierraclub.org/sites/default/files/2025-01/stlouisenergyburdenreportjan2025_0.pdf
 tracts throughout the state, and a close look at St. Louis reveals that the most severely energy

burdened communities are clustered tightly in the North side of the city.4 In St. Louis,

predominantly Black census tracts have more than double the energy burden of predominantly

white census tracts.5 In fact, the disparity is so great that in 2025, two-thirds of households with a

high energy burden within the combined boundaries of St. Louis County and St. Louis City were

located in the City of St. Louis.6 The disproportionate burden borne by the customers of this area

suggests that the additional burden of finding safe and reliable transportation to attend public

hearings should not be imposed as well.


          Second, sluggish tornado recovery efforts have seriously disrupted the ability of many

North St. Louis Ameren customers to pay electric bills, creating a pressing need for face-to-face

community engagement on the community’s turf.7 After the 2025 tornado, while the South side of

St. Louis has largely been rebuilt, many in the North side of St. Louis who had their homes

destroyed have still not moved back in.8 A community struggling to get back on its feet after facing

compounding disasters at least deserves a chance to tell Ameren how it would be impacted by

5609490/REVISED+EJ+Report+with+cover+03122026.pdf (“Central parts of the City – where average
home values near $700,000 – have seen relatively quick and effective cleanup compared to neighborhoods
north of Delmar, where average home values are less than $50,000. As efforts to repair North City move
along at a snail’s pace, residents are concerned that the region may never fully recover.”). Id.


                                                    2
 proposed double-digit rate increases, increases that could very well be devastating to people living

in the North side of St. Louis.


       Therefore, Sierra Club requests that the Commission grant the Consumers Council of

Missouri’s Motion for Additional Local Public Hearing in the City of St. Louis.9 Sierra Club

agrees with Consumers Council that such a public hearing would be well-attended, and adds that

that would be particularly true of a meeting in North St. Louis specifically, due to the

longstanding energy issues that the community has been vocal about needing addressed.




9
